name: Doru Fofana-Câmpeanu
role: Chop shop operator and vehicle parts broker
location: The Stockyard, operates from a leased bay in the Geartown industrial fringe
description:
Doru is nineteen years old and already has the hands of someone twice his age — scarred across the knuckles, always traced with grease that soap only partially removes, with a slight tremor in the left index finger from a pneumatic press accident last year that he never had properly treated. He is tall and lanky, still growing into himself, with warm brown skin, close-cropped natural hair, and a permanent squint from years of working under inadequate lighting. He has cat ear geneware — gray-tipped, slightly mobile — that he got at sixteen because all his friends were getting mods and it seemed like the thing to do; they're more expressive than he intends them to be, flattening when he's stressed in ways he can't control. He wears coveralls in various states of destruction and is almost always holding a tool.

He did not plan to be running a chop shop at nineteen. He planned to be doing legitimate Ferrogate maintenance, for which he has genuine talent, but the apprenticeship application was rejected twice — once for a juvie citation he got at fourteen, once for reasons that were given as 'candidate pool volume' and which he suspects have more to do with his address. The shop fell into his hands when its previous operator left Meridian 88 in a hurry and owed Doru's uncle a favor. He's good at the work. He's learning the business side faster than is comfortable. He is not yet sure if he's the kind of person who ends up staying in this life.

core_fears: becoming someone he can't get out of being
something bad happening to Bolt or Rust because of his decisions
core_desires: a legitimate path that doesn't require pretending none of this happened
recognition that he's actually good at something
coping_mechanisms: mechanical work as total absorption — when he's in a vehicle he stops thinking about everything else
deflects serious conversation with technical talk
blind_spots: underestimates how visible his operation is to Ferrogate Transit's security division, which has been logging the bay for eight months
psychology.secret: He has been sending monthly payments to Ferrogate Transit's anonymous tip line about a rival chop operator in the Stockyard — not because he has a moral objection but because it keeps enforcement attention directed away from his bay. He tells himself this doesn't make him an informant. He is not certain of this.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Mechanical jargon mixed with Stockyard slang. Gets more articulate when talking about engines than about anything else. Short sentences.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast and clipped when busy, which is always. Trails off when uncertain. Gets oddly precise when explaining technical things.
verbal_tics: explains technical details at length when nervous as a deflection
example_lines: 'It's fine. The coupler seal was degraded anyway, that's not from the drop, that's from mileage. Basically you're lucky you brought it here because another hundred ks and you'd have lost the whole drive assembly.'
'I don't ask where vehicles come from. I mean — I have an idea. But I don't ask. That's — it's fine. It's how the bay works.'

story_hooks: Ferrogate Transit's security division is about to move on the bay — Doru needs advance warning and someone who can help him think through whether to run, comply, or negotiate
One of the vehicles that came through the bay had something hidden in the chassis — something that people are now looking for, and those people have found their way to Geartown
narrative_function: Local color and access point for vehicle-related needs; represents the younger generation being funneled into criminal work by structural exclusion; potential for redemption arc or darker trajectory depending on story pressure; information source on what's moving through the Stockyard
augmentations: Cat ear geneware (gray-tipped, mobile, involuntary expressiveness); basic subdermal impact absorption in both hands (installed after the press accident, budget grade)
daily_life: At the bay by 0600, works until the light fails or later. Takes in vehicles — stolen, crashed, or unwanted — and disassembles them for parts with two teenage assistants he calls Bolt and Rust. Spends evenings running the parts ledger and doing client pickups. Eats terribly.
affiliation: Loose affiliation with the Geartown Strippers, a neighborhood crew; owes ongoing tribute to a mid-level Stockyard fence named Brecko Asimov-Ngozi

decision_rules: don't take anything from Tier 4 or above — too much heat
keep Bolt and Rust out of anything that could get them cited
escalation_ladder: does the work and doesn't ask questions
gets quiet and evasive when something is wrong
redirects to technical topics to avoid confrontation
tries to give back whatever is causing the problem
flees the bay if things go physical — he's not a fighter

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Cautious and professional, hides behind technical discussion, takes a while to make eye contact
interpersonal_modes.friends: Genuinely warm and generous with his skills — will fix things for free for people he likes, gives his honest opinion, terrible at emotional conversations but tries

stress_responses.low: Works faster, takes on more disassembly than necessary
stress_responses.medium: Cats ears go flat, he talks more about mechanical details, deflects
stress_responses.high: Goes completely quiet, hands stop moving, makes a decision very fast and then executes it without discussion

contradictions: Has a genuine ethical core that keeps asserting itself inside a profession that doesn't reward ethics; is simultaneously the most and least cynical person in any room he's in
habits: names every vehicle that comes through the bay before disassembly — 'it just feels right'
keeps a running list of parts his operation has produced taped inside his locker, not for inventory but as a record
leaves a small tool as an offering at the E.L.F. that lives in the bay's main breaker panel
breaking_points: Bolt or Rust getting hurt because of his operation; being formally categorized as an informant by the Geartown Strippers

cyberware_inventory.name: Subdermal impact absorption, both hands (budget grade)
cyberware_inventory.description: Subdermal impact absorption, both hands (budget grade)

timeline.event: 2181 — Born in the Stockyard to a family with two generations of Ferrogate maintenance work
2195 — Juvie citation for unauthorized vehicle entry
2198 — Second application rejected; uncle arranges transfer of chop bay
2199 — Pneumatic press accident, left index finger; begins tipping Ferrogate security about rival operation
2200 — Bay under passive surveillance by Ferrogate Transit security division
